rationale: PINS protobuf's whole symbol and relationship contract — the FP-family surface every consumer of this analyzer depends on — against a source file that exercises each construct the language has, and asserts the NEGATIVE controls as carefully as the positive ones. Expectations are derived by reading this file and the protobuf declaration forms, not from an analyzer run. The specific claims under test, each of which is a place a protobuf analyzer can plausibly go wrong: (1) a message is a `class`, an enum is an `enum`, a service is an `interface` and an rpc is a `method` — protobuf has no class/interface/inheritance, so these are MAPPINGS and a reader who assumed the native names would read the wrong shapes; (2) a field's type produces a `uses` edge to a type THIS package declares, and a SCALAR produces none, because `string` is a keyword rather than a declaration; (3) a fully qualified reference with no leading dot still resolves absolutely, so `google.protobuf.Timestamp` lands on itself and not on `demo.v1.google.protobuf.Timestamp` — a dotted name is written fully qualified in practice, and prefixing the package yields a type that exists in no file; (4) a map's VALUE is a reference but a scalar map value is not, and the map's key type is never a reference; (5) a oneof's fields stay members of the MESSAGE and carry `metadata.oneof`, because a field number lives in the message's own space and `msg.field` is how every protobuf tool names it — the oneof itself is a `union` reached from the message, and there is deliberately no second `contains` edge from the oneof to its fields; (6) an rpc's request and response BOTH produce uses edges, and the grammar gives them the same node type with no field name, so they are told apart by position; (7) a file-level `import` is an import, and `import option` — the editions feature-import — is one too, because the pinned grammar had to be patched to accept it.

the field's OWN line, one inside the oneof body — a reader that attributed a oneof field to the oneof's line would pass a one-field oneof and fail here

expectRelationships.note: an unqualified reference to a type this file's package declares
a DOTTED name with no leading dot still resolves absolutely. Prefix the package and this becomes demo.v1.google.protobuf.Timestamp, a type that exists in no file.
the oneof is a union reached from the message
the oneof's field is a member of the MESSAGE
the request type again; the response is also User, on the same line, and the two are told apart by POSITION because the grammar gives both the same node type

expectRelationshipCount.note: request AND response, both User. Exactly two: a reader that emitted one per rpc, or one per distinct type, would report 1 and be wrong in opposite directions.

forbidRelationships.note: DELIBERATELY absent. A oneof's fields are members of the message, and the oneof is reached FROM the message; there is no second contains edge from the oneof to its fields. Membership and grouping are different relations, and overloading `contains` to mean both would make one edge mean two things. The grouping is recorded as `metadata.oneof` on each field instead.
`string` is a scalar KEYWORD. There is no `string` declaration to point at, so a uses edge here would reference something that does not exist.
the map's VALUE is `string`, a scalar, so the map field produces no uses edge. The key type is a scalar by specification and is never a reference.
protobuf has NO inheritance. A field of type Role is a reference (`uses`), not an implementation of an interface, and an `implements` edge here would invent a language feature that does not exist.

forbidSymbols.name: Timestamp
forbidSymbols.note: an imported type is a reference target, not a declaration. `import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto"` makes the type reachable; it does not make this file the place it is declared, and publishing it as a symbol would duplicate the declaration that lives in the imported file.

forbidSymbols.name: google.protobuf.Timestamp
forbidSymbols.note: same reason, at the qualified spelling. The reference is the RELATIONSHIP's target, not a symbol of this file.

forbidSymbols.name: java_package
forbidSymbols.note: a file-level option is file METADATA, not a declaration. It is a directive about code generation, not a type, a message or a field.
